verdict.rationale: Algolia documents InstantSearch UI libraries for building front-end search interfaces and typo tolerance that works 'while typing'. Community reports back up the speed claim: a team moved to Algolia 'mainly for speed', others call it 'blazing fast', and DocSearch users praise its 'instant results'. However, no first-party doc in the pack states millisecond latency or explicitly describes per-keystroke result updates, and one HN user reports occasional slowness. missing for 10: first-party documentation of millisecond response times, explicit documentation of as-you-type/per-keystroke querying, independent latency benchmarks

support.subject: As a developer, I can deliver as-you-type instant search with millisecond responses so results update on every keystroke

citations.quote: InstantSearch.js is an open source UI library for vanilla JS that lets you build a search interface in your frontend app.
Typo tolerance lets users make mistakes while typing but still find the they’re looking for.
If your subscription includes a Distributed Search Network, this ensures that requests are sent to servers closest to users.
A team moved to Algolia mainly for speed, saying Elasticsearch and Solr could not compete.
A team searching about 1.5M US nonprofits finds Algolia blazing fast
